title: Applicability and Availability of Advance Care Planning Documents in Emergency Care for Critically Ill Patients Lacking Decision-Making Capacity – A Prospective Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
summary:
When people become seriously ill or injured, they may no longer be able to make decisions about their medical treatment. In these situations, advance directives, healthcare powers of attorney, and other advance care planning documents can help healthcare professionals respect patients' wishes. However, it is unclear how often these documents are actually available in emergency departments and whether they provide useful guidance for treatment decisions.

The AVANTI study investigates how often such documents are available for critically ill or injured patients who are unable to make their own medical decisions. Emergency departments across Germany will collect information from routine patient care during a predefined 24-hour period.

The study does not influence medical treatment. Its findings are intended to identify opportunities to improve how patients' wishes are considered in emergency situations.
conditions: Limited availability and applicability of advance care planning documents in critically ill emergency department patients lacking decision-making capacity

interventions.name: Prospective, non-interventional observation of all eligible adult high-risk patients lacking decision-making capacity in participating German emergency departments during a predefined 24-hour study period. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Treatment in a participating German emergency department during the predefined 24-hour study period.
- High-risk patient outside the resuscitation room (Manchester Triage System: orange or red; Emergency Severity Index: level 1 or 2) or treatment in a trauma or non-trauma resuscitation room.
- Lack of decision-making capacity at the time of initial emergency department care, as assessed by the treating team.
Exclusion criteria:
- Age below 18 years.
- Presence of decision-making capacity at the time of initial emergency department care.
- Repeated presentation of the same patient during the study period (only the first encounter will be included).
